newsitem.title: USA: Sen. Pressler loses key seat to Democrat in S.Dakota.
newsitem.headline: Sen. Pressler loses key seat to Democrat in S.Dakota.

text.p: Democratic Congressman Tim Johnson unseated three-term incumbent Republican Sen. Larry Pressler in one of the hardest-fought races in Tuesday's election.
With at least 40 percent of precincts reporting, Johnson was leading Pressler by 52 percent to 48 percent.
Pressler, chairman of the Senate Commerce Committee and a key player in shaping new telecommunications law during the last session of Congress, conceded defeat.
Johnson thanked jubilant supporters and said one of his first priorities in Washington would be to revisit the new Farm Law, an influential piece of legislation in this mostly rural Plains state.
"I don't want to gut it but augment it with a longer-term safety net," said Johnson, who will join Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle as the state's other Democratic Senator.
South Dakota voters appeared unable to stomach reports that Pressler spent campaign funds on personal expenditures, including extravagant dinners and accommodations.
He was also accused of using his chairmanship to raise a huge amount of money from political action committees.
"It was Larry's time to go," said George Cunningham, an aide to former Senator George McGovern. "He was spending wildly and foolishly and lost touch with South Dakota."
Pressler, in turn, charged that Johnson was "too liberal" for the state.
